sections.name: Electronics
sections.experimental_note: The electronics are early and changing a lot. Only build these if you have the experience to adapt as the design moves.

changes.name: Replace prototype C-channel supports
changes.description: Replace the current C-channel legs, feet, and leg extensions. These prototype parts work, but they are unstable and will be replaced with improved designs.

changes.name: Widen the C-channel output guide
changes.description: Update the output guide so large pieces that are still within specification can pass through the C-channel exit.

changes.name: Make the camera extension official
changes.description: The camera extension was a prototype and needs to be made official. The finished design should also force the camera into the correct orientation.

changes.name: Mechanically retain the camera LED strips
changes.description: Update the Camera & LED insert so the LED strips are mechanically retained instead of depending on their adhesive. Integrated clips would be a good approach.

changes.name: Secure the Mean Well 24V PSU box cap
changes.description: Improve the Mean Well 24V enclosure because the current cap can pop off too easily. Redesign the cap retention so it locks securely in place.

changes.name: Fix the interface bracket fit
changes.description: Added 0.2 mm clearance on every side of the horizontal aluminum spoke.

changes.name: Fix bulk cap dovetail
changes.description: Increased the dovetail clearance so the bulk cap slides onto the stator more easily and seats without excessive force.

changes.name: Improve the interface bracket design
changes.description: Make the screws for the vertical aluminum extrusion easier to install and remove the interface bracket's unnecessary bulk.

changes.name: Reverse chute door
changes.description: Move the chute door to the other side so the flap closes the open funnel hole. This affects the chute as a whole and all of its parts.

changes.name: Make bin retainers snap on
changes.description: Redesign the left and right bin retainers to snap on and remove their screen holes. Each retainer currently uses two screws, two nuts, and two washers, so this could eliminate roughly 200 purchased pieces from a machine build.

changes.name: Lock the overhead camera mount
changes.description: It would be ideal to lock the overhead camera mount in place completely.

changes.name: Update interface lazy-Susan fasteners to M5
changes.description: Update the four printed parts in the top and bottom interface lazy-Susan joints from M4 to M5 countersunk screws and matching M5 heat-set inserts. The upper interface holes are currently too close together and should be corrected as part of the change.

changes.name: Split the top plate into a supported puzzle
changes.description: Divide the top plate into interlocking puzzle-like sections around a single inner structural support ring, so the plate can be made in smaller pieces while keeping primary support around the center.

images.alt: Seven-piece top plate concept with a single structural inner ring
images.caption: Seven-piece top plate concept

changes.name: Keep the classification chamber aligned
changes.description: The classification chamber can rotate out of place too easily. Even passing pieces can push it out of alignment, which shifts the camera detection zones. A more secure rotational lock would be a useful improvement.

changes.name: Keep the interface spacer in its slot
changes.description: The interface spacer falls off the aluminum profile it slots into too easily. Improve its retention so it stays seated during handling and assembly.

assemblies.name: Light post
assemblies.description: The feeder light post: post, cap, and cap adapter. 2 per machine. Bolts to a C-channel NEMA bracket.

joining.note: The two [[hw:scr-m3-20-cs]] screws that join the post to the NEMA bracket thread straight into the printed post — no insert, no nut.

assemblies.name: External distribution-frame bracket
assemblies.description: Three parts that bolt together into one external bracket. 6 per distribution frame (per layer), plus a set per interface. The cover clips on and takes no screws.

joining.note: All four [[hw:scr-m5-16-shcs]] are designed to self-tap: 2 hold the side to the bottom vertical, 2 hold the assembly to the vertical extrusion. No nuts and no inserts anywhere in this bracket.

assemblies.name: Fixed upper section
assemblies.description: The interface's fixed upper section: the upper-fixed-section plate, its ribs (5 plain + 1 with the limit-switch gap), and the big spacer. 1 per interface. Each rib takes 2 × [[hw:scr-m5-16-shcs]] into the plate; the screw that ties it to its bracket's extrusion belongs to the interface above.

joining.note: Both of each rib's [[hw:scr-m5-16-shcs]] thread straight into the printed upper fixed section — no insert, no nut.

assemblies.name: Cable clamp
assemblies.description: Inner + outer ribbon cable clamp; the two halves clamp together around the cable and the pair bolts to the top interface chute mount.

assemblies.name: Classification chamber
assemblies.description: The classification chamber: the dome, the finned rotor, and the camera & LED insert. All three print white, so the chamber bounces light onto the part instead of absorbing it.

assemblies.name: Chute bearing assembly
assemblies.description: The flap's bearing assembly: left + right bearing holders, the race between them, and the covers. Carries 10 M3 inserts and the two flap bearings, one screw per insert: 6 M3 × 8 hold the covers to the holders (3 each), 4 hold the holders to the race (2 each).

assemblies.name: Servo adapter (MG995)
assemblies.description: MG995 servo adapter: servo side + flap side.

assemblies.name: Servo assembly (MG995)
assemblies.description: The MG995 servo in its bracket: lower arm, side arm, cover, housing. Bolts to the chute core's two arm inserts as a unit.

assemblies.name: Overhead camera mount
assemblies.description: Camera mount for the C-channels. 2 per machine, each hanging off two ~1 ft steel rods.

assemblies.name: Layer connector
assemblies.description: Pair of connectors. 1 of each per layer + 1 of each per bottom interface.

assemblies.name: Chute limit switch
assemblies.description: Interface limit switch: printed dowel pin, housing, hammer, and the switch itself. Bolts to the interface frame as a unit.

assemblies.name: Cable cage
assemblies.description: Six cable cage brackets (5 regular + 1 cable mount) stacked with the ribbon cable clamp. Also sandwiches the laser-cut cage top and bottom plates, which are not in the parts registry yet.

assemblies.name: Orange Pi 5 Housing
assemblies.description: Housing for the Orange Pi 5. Parts and print details are coming soon.

assemblies.name: basically Embedded Control Board Housing
assemblies.description: Housing for the basically Embedded Control Board. Parts and print details are coming soon.

assemblies.name: Meanwell 24V PSU box
assemblies.description: Enclosure for the Meanwell 24V power supply: back mount, connections plate, and cap, screwed to the supply's own case.

assemblies.name: Camera extension
assemblies.description: Classification-channel camera extension for the 4K camera module: the 50 mm extension tube, its mount, and the camera. 1 per machine.

assemblies.name: Pico with headers
assemblies.description: The Raspberry Pi Pico with 2.54 mm header pins fitted, so it can seat in the PCB. The board ships bare — the pins are a separate purchase.

joining.note: Every pin solders into the Pico's through-holes. Nothing here presses or clips together.

assemblies.name: Sorter V2
assemblies.description: The whole machine: feeder on top, interface, the distribution layers between the interfaces, and the bottom interface.

assemblies.name: Feeder
assemblies.description: Feeder + classification channel. Everything above the interface.

assemblies.name: Interface
assemblies.description: The interface between the feeder and the distribution layers. Its lazy Susan sandwiches the upper fixed section and the chute mount, 4 × [[hw:scr-m4-12-cs]] a side, and the plywood top plate bolts down onto the six brackets' inserts.

assemblies.name: Distribution layer
assemblies.description: One distribution layer between the interfaces: frame, chute, bin retainers, funnels, bins. Each bin retainer takes 2 × [[hw:scr-m5-12-shcs]] into a [[hw:tnut-m5-2020]].

assemblies.name: Bottom interface
assemblies.description: The bottom interface / lazy Susan level. Carries two chutes.

assemblies.name: Chute
assemblies.description: One chute: the core plus its door module, funnel brackets, connectors, and PCB. Every screw here lands in one of the chute core's 18 M3 inserts.

assemblies.name: Flap module
assemblies.description: The chute's flap: the door itself, the bearing assembly it swings on, and the servo that drives it.

assemblies.name: Chute PCB
assemblies.description: The layer adapter board, screwed onto the chute core's four PCB inserts.

assemblies.name: C-channel drive
assemblies.description: One C-channel drive unit: stator, NEMA bracket, output gear, gear train and stepper. 4 per machine — 3 in the feeder plus the classification channel's. Screw joints: 4 × [[hw:scr-m3-12-cs]] hold the NEMA bracket to the stator; 3 × [[hw:scr-m3-16-shcs]] hold the stepper to the NEMA bracket; 1 × [[hw:scr-m3-8-shcs]] clamps the input gear to the motor shaft flat; 6 × [[hw:scr-m3-8-cs]] attach the output gear to the rotor, one per spoke (the light post's 2 × [[hw:scr-m3-20-cs]] into the NEMA bracket live on the light-post assembly). The rotor differs by location (faceted in the feeder, finned in the classification chamber), so it is not part of this node.

assemblies.name: Chute Stepper Gearing
assemblies.description: The printed drive and idler gearing that transfers motion from the NEMA 23 chute stepper. The idler gear is retained on the bracket by 1 × [[hw:scr-m3-35-bhcs]] with a [[hw:washer-m3-15]] under the head, spanning the bearing bore; the low head keeps it clear of the limit switch hammer.

assemblies.name: Chute stepper NEMA 23 mount
assemblies.description: The NEMA 23 stepper on its interface bracket. 1 per interface.

assemblies.name: Chute stepper drive gear
assemblies.description: The chute stepper drive gear with its 8 mm bore timing pulley. 1 per interface.

assemblies.name: Interface chute gear + mount
assemblies.description: The chute gear screwed down onto the top interface chute mount — two sections of the split spur gear that become one turning unit.

assemblies.name: Distribution frame
assemblies.description: The frame of one distribution layer: six external brackets, the crossbeams between them, and the 90° brackets. The aluminum extrusion it is built on is sized on the framing tab, not listed here.

assemblies.name: Control board mount
assemblies.description: The basically Embedded Control Board standing off its bracket. The printed bracket is not in the parts registry yet.

assemblies.name: Orange Pi mount
assemblies.description: The Orange Pi 5 standing off its bracket. The printed bracket is not in the parts registry yet.

assemblies.name: Electronics
assemblies.description: The three boxes that bolt to the frame: the PSU, the control board, and the Orange Pi. Each takes 2 × [[hw:scr-m5-shcs-tbd]] — nobody has measured the length yet.

assemblies.name: Interface bracket
assemblies.description: One interface bracket with its spacer, bolted onto its vertical extrusion. 6 per interface.

assemblies.name: Bottom lazy Susan
assemblies.description: The bottom interface's lazy Susan: the static half, the chute mount that spins on it, the extrusion mounts, and the bearing itself. Bolted through 4 × [[hw:scr-m4-12-cs]] a side, same as the top interface's.

hardware.name: M3 × 6 mm countersunk
hardware.description: Secures the limit switch hammer into the top interface chute mount from below, into the hammer's M3 insert.
hardware.note: The ×1 is the top-interface count (limit-switch hammer). Screws used elsewhere on the machine aren't tallied here yet.

hardware.name: M3 × 10 mm socket/button head
hardware.description: Fastens the outer cable clamp into the top interface chute mount, and the ribbon cable clamp to the cable cage bracket.
hardware.note: The ×3 is the top-interface count (2 cable clamp, 1 ribbon clamp). Screws used elsewhere on the machine aren't tallied here yet.

hardware.name: M3 × 8 mm countersunk
hardware.description: The workhorse M3 screw — used all over the machine wherever a flush head is wanted.

hardware.name: M3 × 8 mm socket head
hardware.description: Clamps the C-channel input gear (12T) to the flat of the NEMA 17 shaft. 1 per C-channel.
hardware.note: Head type and length measured off the input-gear STL: the boss carries a Ø2.80 mm hole parallel to the shaft, 3.61 mm off the axis, opening into the Ø4.87 mm bore; the head sits in a Ø6.40 mm × 2.7 mm counterbore, which is a cap-head counterbore rather than a countersink. At 8 mm the head seats and about 6 mm of thread is left in the plastic.

hardware.description: The long M3 countersunk. Used all over the machine.

hardware.name: M3 × 20 mm countersunk
hardware.description: Joins the C-channel light post to the NEMA bracket. Threads straight into the printed post — no insert, no nut.

hardware.name: M3 × 16 mm socket/button head
hardware.description: Bolts the NEMA 17 stepper to the NEMA bracket. 3 per C-channel.

lasercut.name: Cable cage top
lasercut.description: Top plate of the cable cage. Has a keyed cutout for easy insertion/removal of the interface.

handcut.blurb: A regular hexagon, same outline as the bottom plate. Lays out from a rectangle with a tape measure: the centre is one big Ø177 mm drilled-and-jigsawed hole, six mounting holes sit on a 175 mm-radius bolt circle, and a small keyed notch is drilled at each end.

lasercut.name: Cable cage bottom
lasercut.description: Bottom plate of the cable cage.

handcut.blurb: The same regular-hexagon outline as the top cage, but simpler: one big Ø177 mm centre hole and six Ø5.5 mm mounting holes on a 175 mm-radius bolt circle. No small holes, no notch.

lasercut.name: Top plate
lasercut.caption: The machine's hexagonal top plate; the interface mounts under it.
lasercut.description: Machine top plate. Has 5 cable holes and holes for the main stepper. Does not yet have mount holes for the C-channels.

handcut.blurb: This plate is a regular hexagon — it can be laid out with a tape measure and cut accurately with just a jigsaw and a drill. The five cable slots become single 22 mm (7/8″) drill holes.
